items.text: In Russia, French food company Danone will relinquish control of its dairy food business. The deal could lead to a write-off of up to 978 million dollars. Danone joins a lengthy list of global companies that made costly exits from Russia because of its war in Ukraine. Danone will offload a business that represents about 90% of its operations in the country, and only its infant nutrition business will remain. According to the company, this option is best to ensure long-term business continuity. However, Danone didn’t reveal the business recipient. Many Western consumer goods companies including Nestle and Procter&Gamble continue to provide essential food and medicine to Russia; however, they face increasing pressure from consumers and activists to cut all work with the country. Difficult words: relinquish (to give up), write-off (a cancellation from the company as a loss of money), offload (to get rid of something that you don’t want by giving or selling it to someone else). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Since the war in Ukraine started, many companies left Russia, even though their exits cost them a lot of money. On Friday, French company Danone said that it would stop its dairy food business in Russia. Danone will sell about 90% of its business in the country, and it will keep only factories which make infant food. Danone has not said who will buy its business, but the company said that the loss could be up to 978 million dollars. Many Western food companies still have business in Russia; examples are Nestle and Procter&Gamble. They face a lot of criticism from customers and organizations who want them to leave Russia as soon as possible. Difficult words: dairy food (products from milk), infant (a baby), criticism (an explanation that you don’t like something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Danone is a French food company. It has business in Russia. On Friday, Danone says that it will leave Russia. Many countries stop their business in Russia. The reason is the war in Ukraine. Companies lose a lot of money to stop their business. They still do it. They think that it is the right thing to do. Danone will sell 90% of its dairy food business in Russia. Danone does not say who will buy the business. The sell will cost the company about 978 million dollars. Danone will continue to make infant food in Russia. Some other big food companies still have business in Russia. They are companies like Nestle and Procter&Gamble. Many people and organizations criticize them. They say that these companies must stop their business in Russia. Difficult words: dairy food (things like cheese, yogurt, or milk), infant (a baby), criticize (an explanation that something is bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After Hurricane Ian struck Florida, a lot of debris remained on roadsides. These places collected water, and mosquitoes laid their eggs there. Soggy areas with standing water provide a perfect breeding ground for mosquitoes to lay their eggs. In places with moving water, fish and other animals eat the baby mosquitoes. Officers work continuously to control the situation. They do surveillance , trapping, and other analysis, and then they treat the mosquitoes on the ground and from the air. However, days of rain changed the landscape, and the insects have new places to breed. Officers need to monitor the new places and deal with them. The hurricane also contaminated waterways, and the excess water led to mold in low-lying areas, especially inside structures. People are in the middle of an enormous cleanup, and officers encourage them to try to set the garbage so it won’t collect water. Difficult words: soggy (wet and soft), surveillance (close observation), contaminate (to make something less pure or poisonous). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hurricane Ian hit Florida in September, and many places remained wet. These places became perfect for mosquitoes to lay their eggs. Mosquitoes don’t usually lay eggs in lakes and similar places because fish would eat them. Now, many normally dry places are wet. No fish are in these places, and they are safe for mosquitoes. So many mosquitoes are in Florida that a special team has to monitor the situation and find new wet areas. People kill mosquitoes from planes, but this doesn’t completely stop the breeding . People are cleaning up their homes, and streets are full of debris . Officers ask people to set the garbage so that water cannot collect there. Difficult words: monitor (to watch and check something), breed (to make babies), debris (pieces of something broken or destroyed). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hurricane Ian hits Florida in September. It leaves many places wet. These places are perfect for mosquitoes . Mosquitoes don’t lay eggs in lakes or ponds. Fish are there. They eat the eggs. Mosquitoes lay eggs in places without fish. Many places have water in Florida now. Many places also have mosquitoes now. A special team tries to solve the problem. They monitor new wet places. They kill mosquitoes from planes. Officers ask people for help. People put garbage in the streets. Water can stay in things such as toilets or sinks. People need to be careful They need to set the garbage so water falls out. Difficult words: mosquito (a small insect or bug which bites people, and it drinks their blood), monitor (to watch and check something), garbage (things which people throw away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Inflation in Argentina could hit 100% this year, which is the sharpest rise in prices since a period of hyperinflation around 1990. This extreme rise happened as the world is fighting to tame soaring prices. Many people are struggling to survive. At a garbage dump outside Buenos Aires, men waded through piles of waste to find usable clothing and even food; they sort cardboard, plastic, and metal to sell it later. Twice as many people come to the dump or trade their belongings in barter clubs. People have no money left, and they’re so desperate that their only choice is to barter. People exchange things like old clothes for a bag of flour or pasta. A century ago, Argentina was one of the world’s richest countries; however, in recent years, several economic crises happened, and the country has struggled to control inflation. Difficult words: hyperinflation (a very high and out-of-control increase in prices), tame (to make something easier to control), barter (to exchange things or services without money). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A hundred years ago, Argentina was one of the richest countries in the world. Since that time, its situation changed and it’s currently going through a big crisis. Several crises happened in recent years, but this problem is the worst. Experts say that inflation could reach 100%. Things were so expensive that many people have no money at all. Many men come to a garbage dump outside Buenos Aires, and they spend all day searching through mountains of waste. They pick cardboard, plastic, metal, and even food. They hope that they will be able to sell or trade the things for something else. In 2001, Sandra Contreras opened a barter club where people could trade things. Now, it’s full of people again, and they often trade old clothes for food. Difficult words: inflation (the situation when prices are rising, and people can buy less for the same amount of money), garbage dump (a place where people leave waste and material which they don’t need anymore), barter club (a place where people can exchange things without using money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A hundred years ago, Argentina is a very rich country. The situation is different now. Many crises happen in recent years. Now, the crisis in Argentina is very big. Inflation in Argentina can be 100% this year. Inflation means that everything is getting more expensive. People can buy less for the same money. People have only little money now in Argentina. Many men go to garbage dumps . They spend 12 hours there. They look for cardboard, plastic, metal, and even food. They sell what they find. Many people also go to barter clubs. They are places to exchange things. People need no money. They usually trade old clothes for food. Difficult words: crisis (a difficult or dangerous time), garbage dump (a place to leave things and materials which people don’t need anymore), exchange (to give something to someone and get something from him in return). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The world uses a lot of steel, and the process to make steel releases more planet-warming gases than all of India does in a year. The process to make steel has stayed similar to the process from thousands of years ago. The process burns cobs of coal with iron ore from mines. A violent chemical reaction uses carbon from coal to remove unwanted oxygen from the iron ore, which releases iron metal. This process produces billions of tons of carbon dioxide. A Colorado-based company Elektra says it found a solution to that problem. Its solution uses renewable electricity from solar panels or wind turbines instead of coal, and it powers the removal of oxygen from iron ore through electricity. Such a reaction can run at a cooler temperature, and it cuts 90% of the emissions to make steel. Difficult words: cob (a small mass of something), ore (a rock or soil that contains metal), renewable (natural energy sources that are always available). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People make iron when they burn coal with iron ore . A chemical process uses carbon from coal, and it removes oxygen from the iron ore. People started to make steel thousands of years ago, and the process changed only a little. Steel makes billions of tons of gas and smoke, which are more than India makes in one year. A company in California, US, makes iron in a new way. This process makes almost no gas or smoke. The process doesn’t use coal but electricity from solar panels and wind power. The process happens at much lower temperatures, and it lowers pollution by 90%. Difficult words: ore (rock or soil with metal in it), remove (to take something away), steel (a strong grey material, which people make from iron). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Iron is a hard grey metal. People get it from iron ore. They dig it from the ground. They make steel when people add carbon to iron. Steel is even stronger than iron. People use steel to make machines or buildings. People need coal to make iron. People burn the coal. The process takes oxygen from iron. This produces a lot of pollution. It is very bad for the planet. An American company has a new way to make iron. The process doesn’t need coal. It uses electricity from the sun and wind. This lowers pollution by 90%. Difficult words: ore (rock or soil with metal in it), carbon (a chemical which is in all living things, coal, and oil), coal (a black or brown rock which people burn). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Hong Kong, people sold a rare pink diamond for 49.9 million dollars, and it set a world record for the highest price per carat for a diamond sold at auction. The 11.15-carat Williamson Pink Star diamond was auctioned by Sotheby’s Hong Kong, and its original estimate was 21 million dollars. It was the second largest pink diamond to appear at auction, and its name comes from two legendary pink diamonds. The first one is the 23.60-carat Williamson diamond that Queen Elizabeth II got as a wedding gift in 1947. The second diamond is the 59.60-carat Pink Star diamond that sold for a record 71.2 million dollars at auction in 2017. Pink diamonds are among the rarest and most valuable of the colored diamonds. Of all the diamonds, less than 3% are classified as colored diamonds, and less than 5% of those are considered predominantly pink. A pink diamond rarely weighs over 10 carats. Difficult words: carat (a unit to measure the weight of diamonds and other precious stones), legendary (very famous and admired), predominantly (mostly). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, a pink diamond called Williamson Pink Star sold in Hong Kong for 49.9 million dollars. The diamond weighed 11.5 carats , and the estimated price was 21 million dollars. It was the second largest pink diamond ever sold at auction, and it set a new record for the price per one carat. Less than 3% of all diamonds are colored diamonds, and only 5% of them are pink. Pink diamonds are very rare and expensive. Usually they are very small, and they don’t weigh more than 10 carats. Williamson Pink Star diamond has its name after two famous pink diamonds. One of them is Williamson diamond, which weighed 23.6 carats, and Queen Elizabeth II got it as a wedding gift. The second one is Pink Star diamond which weighed 59.6 carats, and it sold for 71.2 million dollars at auction in 2017. Difficult words: carat (a unit for weight of diamond, gold, or jewels), estimate (to give an opinion about the price of something), rare (very unusual). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last week, a pink diamond sells at auction in Hong Kong. The diamond weighs 11.5 carats . Experts say that it costs 21 million dollars. Then the diamond sells for 49.9 million dollars. The name of the diamond is Williamson Pink Star. The name comes from the names of two very famous pink diamonds. One diamond is called Williamson. Queen Elizabeth II gets it as a gift. It is for her wedding in 1947. The second diamond is Pink Star diamond. It weighs 59.6 carats. It sells for 71.2 million dollars in 2017. This price is the highest ever. Pink diamonds are very rare . They are very expensive. Most pink diamonds weigh less than 10 carats. Difficult words: auction (a place where people can buy things, and the person who offers the most money, will get the thing), carat (a unit for weight of diamonds, gold, and so on), rare (very unusual). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Earlier this week, Russia launched a massive wave of missile strikes across Ukraine. The strikes were in response to an attack on the Kerch Bridge that links Russia to Crimea. The bridge was an important route and a symbol of Russia’s annexation of Crimea. The Russian president called the attack a terrorist act by Ukraine. Rockets struck Kyiv during morning rush hour, and they hit a major road junction , a power plant, a popular pedestrian bridge, and a park in the city center. Car dash cams captured the moment when missiles struck in Dnipro. A strike in the city of Lviv narrowly missed electrical pylons that served the city. Rockets hit other cities, including Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, and Kharkiv. The Ukrainian president said that Russia’s main targets appeared to be energy infrastructure and civilians. At least 70 rockets hit 12 Ukrainian cities, and 11 people died in the attacks. Difficult words: annexation (grab a piece of land or a country by force or without permission), junction (a place where things meet or join), pylon (a tall tower-like structure that carries cables high above the ground). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Saturday, an explosion destroyed the Kerch Bridge which linked Russia to Crimea. Russia opened the bridge in 2018, four years after it illegally annexed Crimea, and the bridge became a symbol of this event. The Russian president said that Ukraine was responsible for the explosion, and he called it a terrorist attack. Two days later, Russia responded to the attack, and Russian rockets hit 12 Ukrainian cities. In Kyiv, the strike came in the morning, when the streets were full of cars and people. Rockets hit roads, bridges, parks, a government building, and a power plant. In Lviv, rockets missed cables that brought electricity to the city. The Ukrainian president said that Russia’s plan was to hurt people and to damage the energy infrastructure . Difficult words: annex (to take an area of land or a country by force), symbol (a thing that represents something), energy infrastructure (structures and equipment which bring electricity to buildings). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2014, Russia takes Ukrainian Crimea by force. Russia builds a bridge. The bridge links Crimea and Russia. It opens in 2018. Last weekend, an explosion breaks the bridge. The Russian president says that Ukraine causes the explosion. Two days later, Russia attacks several Ukrainian cities. Russian rockets hit for Kyiv, Lviv, and Kharkiv. They hit roads, parks, bridges, a power plant , and other important buildings. In Kyiv, the attack happens in the morning. Many people and cars are in the streets. In Lviv, rockets explode near cables. They bring electricity to the city. The Ukrainian president says Russia wants to hurt people. At least 70 rockets hit the cities. 11 people die. Difficult words: explosion (when something breaks up with a loud noise), power plant (a factory which makes electricity), explode (to break up into pieces with a lot of noise). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last week, the Revolution for Prosperity Party (RFP) won in Lesotho’s election. A millionaire diamond magnate named Sam Matakane created the party in March this year; however, the party emerged as the country’s biggest single party after the election. It doesn’t have a majority in Lesotho’s parliament, so it’ll need other parties to help it change the government. RFP promised a new era of leadership and prosperity in the country with exploitation of natural resources and competitiveness . Lesotho is a landlocked area within South Africa with years of political instability. Since 2017, the current governing party named All Basotho Convention ran the country of 2.14 million people. Difficult words: magnate (a rich and influential businessperson), prosperity (the state of being successful and rich), competitiveness (the ability to be as good or nearly as good as others). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In March this year, a rich diamond businessman created a new political party in Lesotho. The party was called the Revolution for Prosperity, and last week, it won the election. The party didn’t get the majority in Lesotho’s parliament, and it will have to work with other parties to make a new government. The party promised that many things would change, and that Lesotho would become as successful as other countries in the region. Lesotho is a landlocked kingdom in southern Africa, and it became independent from the UK in 1966. 2.14 million people live in the country. After years of many problems in the country, they wish to change the government to have a better future. Difficult words: majority (more than a half), landlocked (when a country is not next to a sea), independent (free from control). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lesotho is a country in southern Africa. It is an enclave in South Africa. 2.14 million people live there. Last week, people in Lesotho vote for a new government. A new party wins. Its name is RFP. A rich businessman makes the party in March. The party promises that many things will change in Lesotho. The party doesn’t get enough power in the parliament. RFP will have to work with other parties. In 1966, Lesotho becomes independent from the UK. The country has many problems. RFP says that its leader will make Lesotho a successful country. He has a lot of business knowledge. Difficult words: enclave (a country which is within another country), party (a political group), independent (with its own government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In north-east Thailand, a mass shooting and stabbing occurred at a nursery on Thursday. During the children’s naptime , a former policeman entered the preschool and opened fire. He killed at least 37 people, including 23 children, some of them as young as two years old. Local people rushed to donate blood at the nearby Nong Lamphu Hospital; meanwhile, the community remained in shock. After the mass shooting, the gunman fled to his home where he killed his wife and child, and then he shot himself. The police fired the 34-year-old man in June for drug use; however, according to Thailand’s prime minister, the man’s motive was unknown. The headteacher said that the attacker’s son also attended the school, and the attacker was always polite and chatty . More than 90 children were usually at the school, but just over 20 were present on Thursday due to bad weather and a school bus breakdown. Difficult words: naptime (a short sleep during the day), chatty (talkative), motive (a reason to do something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, a man entered a nursery in north-east Thailand and fired a gun. He killed and stabbed at least 37 people, and 23 of them were children. The incident happened while the children were sleeping. After the attack, the man ran home to kill his family and himself. Local people rushed to a nearby hospital to donate blood for his victims. The attacker was a 34-year-old man. He was a policeman, but in June, he lost his job because of drug use. Officials don’t know why the man attacked the nursery. People at the nursery said that he was usually friendly and talkative. Normally 90 children were at the nursery, but only around 20 were there on Thursday. Many children didn’t come because of bad weather and a school bus was broken. Difficult words: nursery (a school for very young children and where teachers look after them), stab (to attack someone with a knife), donate (to give something to a person who needs it, usually food or money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man kills 37 people in a nursery in Thailand. The people are teachers and 23 children. The terrible event happens last week. This man is 34 years old. He is a former policeman. He takes drugs. He loses his job. On Thursday, this man walks into the nursery. The children are sleeping. The man kills the teachers and children. Then, the man runs home. He kills his family and himself. Usually, 92 children are at the nursery. On that day, only 20 are there. Some children can’t go to school because the weather is bad. Also, a school bus doesn’t work. Officials don’t know why the man attacks the nursery. People say that the man is friendly and talkative. Difficult words: nursery (a place where young children stay, and teachers look after them), former (happens or be at an earlier time), talkative (a person who likes to talk to others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Prominent Egyptian archaeologists renewed a request to return the Rosetta Stone from the British Museum to Egypt. The Rosetta Stone dates to 196 BC, and Napoleon’s army unearthed it in Northern Egypt in 1793. It bears writings that unlocked the secrets of hieroglyphics and ancient languages and cultures. Since 1802, the stone has been at the British Museum; however, Egyptian archaeologists requested its return in the past. Other Western museums have been returning artifacts that were removed from countries under colonial rule, so archaeologists hope the British Museum will do the same thing. The ethical code of museums is changing, and public involvement is pushing the British government to act. According to some experts, museums will eventually restitute many objects and thus correct history’s mistakes. Difficult words: prominent (important or famous), ethical code (a set of moral principles and standards of an organization), restitute (to return objects that have been stolen or lost). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Rosetta Stone is a piece of black stone from 196 BC. It bears three inscriptions in Greek, Egyptian hieroglyphics, and Egyptian script characters. The Rosetta Stone is very important because people used it to decipher hieroglyphics and learn more about ancient Egypt. In 1793, Napoleon’s army found the stone in Northern Egypt. Since 1802, the stone has been at the British Museum in London. Egyptian archaeologists asked England to return the stone to Egypt, but they didn’t do it. Ideas are changing now, and many museums are returning artifacts to their home countries. Egyptian archaeologists hope that the returns will help their situation, and the Rosetta Stone will finally return to Egypt. Difficult words: inscription (words that someone writes or cuts in something), decipher (to find the meaning of something that is difficult to read or understand), artifact (a very old object). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Rosetta Stone is a black stone. It is more than 2,200 years old. It is very important for archaeologists . On the stone, people write three similar texts. The texts are in different languages. The texts are Egyptian hieroglyphics , Greek, and demotic . The stone helps archaeologists to understand Egyptian hieroglyphics. They can better understand the Egyptian language and culture. In 1793, Napoleon’s soldiers find the stone in Egypt. Since 1802, the Rosetta Stone is at the British Museum in London. Egypt wants the stone back. Many museums are now returning objects to their home countries. Egyptian archaeologists hope that the Rosetta Stone will return to Egypt. Difficult words: archaeologist (a person who studies old objects), demotic (old Egyptian script writing), hieroglyphic (old Egyptian writing with images and sounds for each word or words). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Google’s debut Pixel Watch is jumping into the smartwatch industry already dominated by Apple Watch. The watch is the latest addition to the company’s Pixel collection of digital devices, which includes smartphones, laptops, and tablets. The Pixel Watch will go on sale on October 13, 2022, for 350 dollars, and a model with mobile connections costs an additional 50 dollars. The watch is limited to Android phones, and it enables contactless payments, music control, and turn-by-turn directions. According to Google, the watch is also resistant to water and scratches. The Pixel Watch comes in colors including silver, charcoal, and matte black, and it has 20 different bands in a wide range of colors. It also includes 19 customizable interfaces . Difficult words: debut (a demonstration for the first time), turn-by-turn (a feature where directions are continually presented to the user), interface (a device or program that connects another device or equipment). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

For a long time, Apple Watch controlled the smartwatch market, but now, its biggest rival Google is selling the Pixel Watch. The watch belongs to Google’s Pixel collection , which includes smartphones, laptops, and tablets. The watch has a simple design, and it comes in several different colors. Customers can also choose from 20 different bands . The Pixel Watch costs 350 dollars, and if you want a model to connect to your phone, you will pay 50 dollars more. The watch is for people who have Android phones. They can use the watch to do activities such as to pay in shops or control music. Difficult words: rival (someone who competes in the same activity), collection (a group of things), band (a strip around a person’s wrist). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many people wear a smartwatch. The watch looks normal. It is not normal but a small computer. People can check emails, listen to music, or do sports with it. For a long time, company Apple makes the best smartwatch. It is the Apple Watch. Now, Google makes its first smartwatch. The watch is the Google Pixel Watch. People can choose from different colors and bands . They can connect it with their Android phone. People can pay in shops with the watch. Google Pixel Watch costs 350 dollars. A model to connect to your phone costs 400 dollars. Google Pixel Watch is on sale on October 12, 2022. Difficult words: band (a strip around a person’s wrist), model (a specific type of a product), on sale (sell something in a shop). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After a wildfire swept through Easter Island last week, some of the iconic Moai stone statues suffered irreparable damage. The blaze in Chile’s Rapanui National Park caused several of the statue stones to crack. According to officials, the damage was unmeasurable , and it was impossible to repair the statues because the fire warmed and cracked the stones. A preliminary report from Chile’s Heritage ministry stated that the fire started on Tuesday and burned nearly 150 acres of land. The causes were unknown for the fire and damaged statues. The island is about 3,200 kilometers from the coast of Chile, and its inhabitants carved over a thousand of sacred statues of giant heads centuries ago. It had only recently reopened to tourists after more than two years due to the pandemic. Difficult words: irreparable (impossible to repair or make right again), unmeasurable (impossible to measure), sacred (regarded as very valuable or respected). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, a wildfire damaged the famous stone statues on Chile’s Easter Island. Officials don’t know the fire’s cause or the number of damaged statues. The fire affected nearly 150 acres of land, and officials said that it was impossible to repair the statues because they cracked in the heat. Hundreds of years ago , Indigenous people carved a thousand stone statues that look like heads, and recently, the island became world famous for them. The island closed more than two years ago because of the coronavirus, and it opened to tourists again only a few months ago. Difficult words: indigenous (people who originally lived in a place), carve (to cut a hard material into an object or design), crack (to break into parts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Famous Moai stone statues are on Easter Island. They look like big heads. More than a thousand of statues are on the island. The island belongs to Chile. It is about 3,200 kilometers from Chile. It is in the Pacific Ocean. Hundreds of years ago, indigenous people carve the heads in the stones. Tourists from all the world visit the statues. Last week, a fire starts on the island. It burns almost 150 acres of land. The stone statues get hot. Some statues crack . It is not possible to fix them. Officials don’t know why the fire starts. It is also not clear how many statues are broken. Difficult words: indigenous (people who originally live in a place for a very long time), carve (to cut a hard material into an object), crack (to break into parts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kenyan farmers have been switching from corn to avocado cultivation amid rise in global demand and changes in weather patterns. Many small-scale farmers in Western Kenya have traditionally grown corn; however, they’re focusing on avocados now. Poor sales of corn and weather changes forced the farmers to seek other ways to make money. Avocados get better prices, better yields , and farmers can harvest them continuously for eight months of the year. Kenya is now Africa’s biggest producer of avocados, as it sells about 80,000 metric tons annually. Cleaned and packed avocados are shipped to markets in Europe, mainly Spain and the Netherlands, the Middle East, and elsewhere in Africa. Kenya has also started to sell in the Asian markets, and it became the first African country to export fresh avocados to China. Difficult words: cultivation (the preparation of land to grow crops on it), small-scale (a small amount of people or over a small area), yield (an amount of crop you grow on a farm). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Farmers in Kenya started to grow avocados instead of corn. The reasons were weather changes and avocados make the farmers more money. Sales of corn fell in Kenya, and farmers had to look for other crops to grow. Avocado was perfect because farmers can harvest it for eight months of the year, and its yields are better than corn. In recent years, Kenya became the biggest producer of avocados in Africa. The country exports avocados to Europe, mainly to Spain and the Netherlands. Other big avocado markets for Kenya are in the Middle East and Egypt. In August, Kenya became the first African country to export fresh avocados also to China. Difficult words: harvest (to pick crops or sell animals to eat), yields (the amount of products which a farmer or company produces), export (to send products to another country for sale). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many farmers in Kenya grow corn. The sales are not good. Also, the weather is changing. Farmers look for new plants to grow. Avocados are a good idea. Farmers harvest them for eight months. Avocados bring more money than corn. Many small farmers switch from corn to avocados. They must learn how to grow avocados. Everything is new for them. Kenya is the biggest seller of avocados in Africa. Kenya’s avocados travel to Spain, the Netherlands, Egypt, and the Middle East. In August, Kenya starts to sell to China. The business is risky . Kenya is the first African country to export fresh avocados to China. Difficult words: harvest (to pick crops or sell animals to eat), risky (possible that something bad or dangerous will happen), export (to sell products to another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Observers on Earth can only see one side of the moon because it is tidally locked to our planet, which means that its orbital period is the same as its rotation around its axis . The side which is never visible from Earth is called the dark side of the moon, and recently a camera captured it aboard a NASA satellite. The images show the moon moving across the Pacific Ocean towards North America. However, this was not the first time that humankind could see the dark side, as there were pictures of it back in 1959 during a Soviet mission. Difficult words: observer (a person who observes – watches something), tidal lock (when a side of a moon or a planet always faces another moon or planet), orbital (relating to orbit – the regularly repeated elliptical course of an object), axis (an imaginary line about which something rotates), Soviet (the name for Russian’s government during Communism). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People on Earth can only see one side of the moon because the moon is locked to our planet. There is a side of the moon which you can never see. It is called the dark side of the moon. First images of the side could be seen in 1959 thanks to a Soviet mission. Now, a camera aboard a NASA satellite captured it. It took a series of images. The images show a crater and how the moon moves across the Pacific Ocean towards North America. Difficult words: series (a set), crater (a large space in the ground which looks like a bowl). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

You can watch the moon, but you can see only one side. You cannot see the other side from the earth . This other side is called the dark side of the moon. In 1959, people see it for the first time. Soviets take pictures of it. Now, we have some new pictures. A NASA satellite takes them. Difficult words: earth (our planet), satellite (a machine that goes to space). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A traffic camera captured s tunning footage of a snowy owl in Montreal, Canada. The majestic visitor has delighted viewers with the video gaining over 15,000 likes and 18,000 shares on Facebook. The reason the sighting attracted so much attention is not just the beauty of the video, but also because seeing snowy owls is quite rare, as they tend to inhabit places where humans do not live. Moreover, the snowy owl is an official symbol of Quebec and people protect it from hunters in Canada, though the birds are occasionally killed in collisions with cars, airplanes and utility lines . Difficult words: stunning (amazing), delight (make feel nice, please), majestic (amazing), gain (to get), sighting (seeing), inhabit (live in), utility lines (power lines). The European Parliament approved new rules for the EU to introduce a single charging port for mobile phones, tablets, and cameras by 2024. The rules also apply to laptops in 2026. According to lawmakers, this simple solution will save thousands of tons of electronic waste every year. The change will facilitate the reuse of old electronics, better consumer convenience , reduce unnecessary cost, and save millions of dollars. Old chargers won’t be outlawed , and customers will be able to continue to use existing models. Connectors for Android-based devices will become the standard across the EU; however, Apple will now have to change its charging port for iPhones and other devices. The law also covers e-readers, earbuds, and other technologies, which means that it may impact device makers such as Samsung, Huawei, and others. Difficult words: facilitate (to make easier), convenience (to be easy to do or useful for someone), outlaw (to make something illegal).

A new EU law says that all mobile phones, tablets, and cameras will use the same charging port by 2024. The law will also apply to e-readers, earbuds, and laptops. All devices will use the same port as Android devices. Apple will have to change its charging ports, which upsets the company. In the past, Apple said that changes to the charging ports would cost a lot of money and would be bad for innovation . The new law will save thousands of tons of waste and millions of dollars. The changes will be more convenient for people because they won’t need different chargers for different devices. Difficult words: innovation (new ideas or ways of doing things), waste (things which people throw away), convenient (easy to do or get). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: law (an official rule which people must follow), device (a small electronic machine), charging port (an electronic part to help you give power to a device). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Sunday, Burkina Faso president Paul-Henri Damiba conditionally resigned after last week’s coup . Last weekend, violent protests and clashes happened in the capital city Ouagadougou. Self-declared military leader Captain Ibrahim Traoré agreed to seven stipulations from Damiba. They included to guarantee Damiba safety and security to the soldiers who supproted him. Traoré said that Islamic violence in the country was worsening, and the country was facing an emergency in every industry, from security to health to infrastructure. He asked cabinet ministers to tackle the urgent problems faster, and some people feared his words suggested the country will get help from Russia. According to a close family member, Damiba left the country on Sunday. The coup was the second military coup this year, after Damiba ousted former president Rock Caboret in January; it was the ninth coup since independence from France in 1960. Difficult words: coup (a sudden violent overthrow of a government by a group of people), stipulation (a condition), oust (to force someone to leave a position of power). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The number of attacks by Islamist groups increased in recent months, and the situation in the country was getting worse. Many problems are happening in many areas, from security to healthcare. Traoré agreed with Damiba to protect his soldiers and him, but on Sunday, Damiba left the country to neighboring Togo. This coup was already the second coup this year, and the ninth coup since Burkina Faso became independent from France in 1960. Difficult words: coup (a quick and violent change of government), security (safety from attacks or danger), independent (with your own government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2017, 14-year-old Molly Russel took her own life after she saw extensive images and videos about suicide, depression, self-harm and anxiety. An inquest into Molly’s death concluded that harmful online content was a factor in her death. The girl suffered from depression and online content’s negative effects. She saved 2,100 images on Instagram related to depression, self-harm, and suicide. Since her death, Molly’s father has campaigned tirelessly for better Internet safety, and he welcomed the verdict on Friday. He said that it was time the toxic culprit culture changed at Instagram. He added it was time to protect innocent young people and not allow platforms to make profits from their misery. Several social media experts and representatives heard the inquest; they said that some of Molly’s posts violated the platform’s guidelines, and some of the content on social media shouldn’t be available for a child to see. According to one of the psychiatrists, the chance was very important to make the Internet safer. Difficult words: inquest (an official examination), campaign (organized actions to achieve a goal), culprit (a criminal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Experts confirmed that some of the images and videos were too dangerous for Molly to see, and some of her posts broke the platform’s rules. Difficult words: suicide (to take your own life), self-harm (to hurt yourself intentionally), confirm (to say that something is true or correct). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Indonesia, at least 125 people died, and 180 were injured in a soccer match crush; the incident was one of the world’s worst stadium disasters. In the Malang province, the tragedy unfolded on Saturday after home side Arema FC lost 3-2 to its long-time rival Persebaya Surabaya. Frustrated Arema supporters invaded the pitch, and security responded with tear gas to control the situation. Officials said the crush happened because fans fled the gas to the exit gate where they suffocated . Officials stated that 42,000 tickets had been sold for the match at Kanjuruhan stadium when its capacity was 38,000. Indonesia’s president Joko Vidodo ordered the Football Association of Indonesia to suspend all games in the top League until officials complete an investigation. FIFA, the world soccer’s governing body, requested a report on the incident. In its safety regulations, FIFA specifies that stewards or police shouldn’t carry or use firearms or crowd control gas. Difficult words: rival (a person or team that competes with another in the same activity), suffocate (to die from lack of air), suspend (to stop activity). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Angry fans ran into the pitch , and security wanted to control the crowd, so they fired tear gas. To escape, people ran towards the exits, where some of them suffocated . Officials later said that 42,000 tickets were sold, but the stadium’s capacity was only 38,000 people. Officials started to investigate the incident, and the International Football Association FIFA asked the Indonesian government for a report. According to FIFA’s rules, security at soccer matches mustn’t use weapons or tear gas. Difficult words: pitch (the area where some sports happen), suffocate (to die because of not enough air), capacity (the number of people or things that fit somewhere). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: tear gas (a gas which makes the eyes hurt), exit (a door or gate to leave a place), suffocate (death from not enough air). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Friday, Vladimir Putin said his annexation was irreversible for four occupied regions in Ukraine. He staged referendums in all four regions; however, the international community criticized them as tricks. Reportedly, at some places, soldiers went from door to door to gather people’s votes. By seizing almost a fifth of Ukraine, the Russian president grabbed the most land in Europe since World War II; he added that the people in Ukraine’s Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzia regions would be Russian citizens forever. Putin also demanded Ukraine stop its fight and begin talks; however, he refused to negotiate about the annexation. The US president Joe Biden pledged the United States would never recognize Russia’s claims on Ukraine’s territory, and he said that the US would impose new sanctions on Russia. Difficult words: annexation (the takeover of a piece of land or a country by force or without permission), irreversible (not possible to change), referendum (a vote by the people to make a change in their government). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In some places, soldiers went to people’s homes to get their votes. Putin asked Ukraine to stop fighting and start talks, but he said that the four regions would be part of Russia forever. The US president Joe Biden and other world leaders said that they would never recognize the regions as Russian. Difficult words: annex (to take a piece of land or country by force), referendum (a vote by people about an important thing), recognize (to accept that something is legal or true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People released more than 130 sea turtles into the Gulf Stream , off the North Carolina coast, after they recovered from cold stunning , or hypothermia , brought on by a drastic drop in water temperature. The US Coast Guard helped the North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission to launch the rescue operation after a cold snap in North Carolina sent temperatures below freezing in parts of the state. Over a hundred cold-stunned green sea turtles had been found floating or washed ashore. After spending some time in a rehabilitation facility, people took the turtles 15 to 20 miles offshore to warmer waters where they released them back into the water. As with other reptiles, sea turtles rely on their external environment to regulate their body temperature. Cold stunning occurs when water temperatures drop below 10° Celsius. Difficult words: cold stunning (being dangerously cold), hypothermia (having a very low body temperature), launch (to start), cold snap (a sudden, short period of very cold weather), float (to be carried by water), reptile (a cold-blooded animal like turtles and snakes). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Turtles and other animals, like snakes, are reptiles. These are animals which cannot control their body temperatures. Turtles get cold-stunned when water temperatures drop below 10° Celsius. Difficult words: cold snap (a sudden, short period of very cold weather), cold-stunned (to be so cold that you could die), rehabilitation facility (a place where you can get better).
